guides.wedding-budget-calculator.title: Wedding Budget: Where the Money Actually Goes
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.desc: A realistic wedding budget breakdown by category, with the hidden line items couples miss and a contingency rule that prevents overspend.
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.lead: The venue and catering dominate, but the overrun usually comes from the small unassigned lines: service charges, gratuities, alterations, postage and tax.
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.f1v: Venue, catering and bar typically absorb about half the total
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.f2v: Hold back 5–10% of the total, unallocated
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.f3v: Service charge, tax, gratuities, alterations, postage, tips, parking
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.f4v: Divide the total by confirmed headcount, not invites
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.s1: Build the budget from a per-guest figure backwards: catering and bar scale linearly, while photography, venue hire and attire are largely fixed. That is why cutting ten guests saves real money and cutting the guest list by ten percent after the venue is booked does not. Assign every line an owner and a due date, and keep contingency genuinely unspent.
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.s2: US quotes frequently exclude sales tax and a mandatory service charge of 18–25%, so a headline price can understate the invoice by a quarter; gratuities may be separate again. UK and European quotes more often include VAT, but may itemise corkage, late-licence fees or staffing. In some cultures the families split specific categories by custom rather than by a single shared budget, so agree who pays for what before requesting quotes.
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.s3: The classic mistake is treating the deposit schedule as the budget. Track committed total, not cash paid to date. Also check currency and exchange fees for a destination wedding, and read cancellation clauses before signing — the largest single financial risk is usually a non-refundable venue payment made twelve months out.
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.q1: What is a realistic wedding budget?
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.a1: It varies widely by region and guest count. Build from a per-guest catering figure plus fixed vendor costs, then add tax, service and contingency.
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.a2: Service charges, gratuities, attire alterations, invitation postage, marriage licence, transport, accommodation, vendor meals and post-wedding thank-yous.
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.q3: How much should we keep in reserve?
guides.wedding-budget-calculator.a3: Five to ten percent of the total, left unallocated. It absorbs the small overruns that otherwise compound across every category.
